business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Virgin Polyethylene and Polypropylene Granules

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17) and Beneficial Ownership Information Regulations (SOR/2023-138)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists (FATF, UN, OFAC, FINTRAC), sanctions lists (UN, OFAC, EU, Canadian), and enhanced due diligence per FINTRAC guidelines for medium-risk entities

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language requirements with English transliteration where applicable; no foreign language names without French translation
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government or public authority without approval
Sensitive industry terms requiring ministerial approval if applicable
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Appeal to the Registre des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of rejection, following administrative procedures outlined in the Companies Act

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for non-resident corporations but must comply with address verification and AML requirements; virtual offices are accepted but physical presence may be required for certain filings
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium risk of unannounced inspections for medium-risk entities like petrochemical trading, primarily for compliance verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal consultation and name search fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Quebec corporate setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office setup and virtual office services
AML/CFT compliance screening and reporting setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss 10 (incorporation), 12 (articles), 17 (certificate of incorporation), 77-87 (registered office and records), 104-113 (officers); supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Québec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) filed electronically with REQ together with the initial enterprise registration declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the QBCA; shares may be subscribed without immediate paid-up capital, and no escrow or capital deposit account is required for a Québec business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the share subscriptions recorded in the subscription list and all shares are allotted and issued as fully paid or credited capital. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [address], in the judicial district of [district], Province of Quebec, and that the Registraire des entreprises du Québec be instructed to record the registered office. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [name] be appointed Secretary, and [name] be appointed Treasurer, each to hold office until a successor is elected. RESOLVED, that such officers are authorized to open banking accounts, execute agreements, and complete all necessary regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search and name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online name-search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Québec enterprise registry for the proposed name 'Bulk Petrochemical Polymers Inc.' or a French equivalent. Obtain a nuanced name search report and, if desired, reserve the name for up to 90 days through the REQ online portal. The name must sufficiently distinguish the corporation from existing registered entities and must not contravene public order.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French or bilingual format
Representation or power of attorney, if the filer is not a director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised name with a new search report; REQ’s written refusal identifies the conflicting element, which may be corrected by wording or by obtaining the consent of the prior registrant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of articles of incorporation and initial by-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate secretary or legal counsel; REQ filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in accordance with the QBCA schedule, include any special share provisions, the initial registered office address, the minimum/maximum number of directors, and the list of first directors. Prepare the initial by-laws by private resolution for adoption at the first board meeting.
required_dossiers: Written consent of each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects the filing for incomplete schedules, correct the missing schedule or the director consents and resubmit the same application without restarting the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of articles of incorporation and initial enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), ‘Constitution d’une société par actions’ online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the articles of incorporation through REQ’s secure online platform, provide the initial enterprise registration particulars, and pay the applicable state fee by credit card or online payment. On approval, REQ issues a certificate of incorporation and an enterprise registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a correction notice is issued, access the application in the REQ portal, amend the identified fields, and resubmit before the statutory deadline; refusal may be cured by filing a fresh application with appropriate disclosures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of certificate and registration with tax authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, use the REQ enterprise number to register with Revenu Québec for corporation tax, GST/QST harmonized or separate accounts, and employer payroll accounts if hiring. Register the federal business number with CRA for income tax and payroll deductions through the Business Registration Online service.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing tax account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec rejects the account registration, verify the legal name and enterprise number in the REQ database, correct typographical mismatches, and resubmit; late registration penalties may be avoided by demonstrating good faith and timely submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board of directors meeting and organizational resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written board consent to adopt the by-laws, accept subscriptions, issue shares, fix the registered office, appoint officers, approve a share certificate form, and open a corporate bank account. Maintain the executed minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Minute book, share certificates, and securities register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resolution is later found incomplete, correct the minute book by a supplementary board resolution validly passed under QBCA rules; no re-filing with REQ is required for purely internal governance matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of registered office and director notices with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a declaration of registration / update in the REQ portal confirming the registered office address, the list of current directors, and any restrictions on share transfers. The declaration must be updated within 15 days of any subsequent director or office change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or incomplete declarations are regularized by filing a corrected update; REQ may assess modest late fees, but the corporation may apply for cancellation or reduction of the penalty by showing mitigating circumstances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal occupancy and fire safety compliance verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permit and fire prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the leased office/warehouse use is authorized under the municipality’s zoning and occupancy by-laws. Obtain a fire safety attestation where required by the Québec Fire Safety Code, and verify that the structural floor load can support palletized inventories of virgin polymer granules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal inspection identifies non-compliance, obtain the required permits or engineer’s report and submit a corrective action plan; the municipality will normally release the occupancy certificate once the corrective measures are completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final registrar record review and statutory good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the REQ certificate and public record for accuracy, ensure the articles and registry show the correct corporate name, head office, directors, and officers. Confirm tax account activation and obtain a statement of good standing from REQ for counterparties and banking documentation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any registry detail is erroneous, file a voluntary correction under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; REQ will correct the record retroactively where the error arises from a registry mistake.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no Québec industrial operating permit is triggered for the wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules; the activity is classified as commercial distribution rather than manufacturing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None (wholesale distribution only) — an ordinary municipal occupancy certificate may apply, but no provincial industrial establishment permit is required under the QBCA or the Environment Quality Act for non-manufacturing polymer trading.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required for the storage or distribution in original packaging of virgin polymer granules, because no listed contaminant discharge or prescribed industrial activity is present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC process discharges are generated by the wholesale trading activity; if site drainage occurs, comply with municipal effluent by-laws and any provincial water-quality discharge limits; implement housekeeping controls for plastic dust and pellet spillage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire service for the leased warehouse/office premises, ensure compliance with the Québec Fire Safety Code for storage height, egress and pallet loading, and obtain a CNESST workplace health and safety clearance when employees are first hired; structural load capacity for heavy polymer pallet storage must be documented.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenu Québec as the provincial tax authority for TPS/TVQ with portal at revenuquebec.ca; Canada Revenue Agency for federal matters with portal at canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA via the My Business Account online portal following incorporation. Quebec entities register with Revenu Québec to secure a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and enroll for TPS/TVQ. The process entails submission of articles of incorporation, business registration forms, and supporting documentation through the respective government portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available for Canadian corporations. Canadian Controlled Private Corporations (CCPCs) may elect small business deduction treatment for reduced corporate tax rates. Hybrid mismatch rules are governed by the Income Tax Act and General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TPS/TVQ (Taxe sur les produits et services / Taxe sur les ventes du Québec)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual gross revenue from taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API requirements, or digital stamping. Businesses must issue tax invoices upon request, maintain electronic records, and file periodic TPS/TVQ returns electronically through the Revenu Québec portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services supplied to non-residents outside Canada qualify for zero-rating under the TPS/TVQ regime. For bulk petrochemical polymers, eligibility requires verifiable proof of export, no domestic consumption, and full compliance with customs export formalities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims may result in penalties up to 200% of the evaded tax, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act. Retrospective clawback applies if export status or documentation is deemed insufficient.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation is administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and anti-money-laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no central foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control department.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. No prior exchange-control approval is required for inbound equity investment, trade settlements, dividend remittances, interest payments, royalties, or capital repatriation. Profit remittances are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% absent treaty relief, commonly reduced to 5% for dividends and 10% for interest/royalties under the Canada-U.S. and other income tax treaties). Foreign-currency accounts and external borrowings are unrestricted, provided that documentation supporting the underlying trade obligation and source of funds is retained for bank compliance and Canada Revenue Agency audits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in US dollars or other freely convertible currencies, converted at market rates, or held in foreign-currency accounts at Canadian deposit-taking institutions. The only reporting obligations are the export declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) under the Customs Act and balance-of-payments statistics reporting to Statistics Canada; neither triggers exchange surrender or a forced conversion timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for established Canadian-regulated payment fintechs that hold a FINTRAC money services business (MSB) registration or a Bank of Canada retail payment system provider licence under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Low for offshore electronic-money institutions without a Canadian legal presence or MSB/PSP registration, because they lack direct access to Lynx/ACSS clearing, are generally not recognized as authorized deposit-taking institutions, and face correspondent de-risking. A Canadian subsidiary EMI can support FX conversion and disbursement workflows but cannot replace a tier-1 bank for documentary letters of credit, high-limit CAD settlement, and corporate treasury services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement mandates physical board appearance at account opening; however, Canadian banks are required by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance to obtain reliable customer due diligence. In practice, non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners must either appear in person at a Canadian branch, complete a verified video interview with a bank officer, or provide notarized/certified identity documentation accepted by the bank's enhanced due-diligence unit. Fully remote onboarding is possible only where the bank's risk regime permits it and a complete CDD package is submitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or Global Affairs Canada screening hit against the jurisdiction, a director, or the ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate ownership chart; passport and government-issued photo ID for each director and BO; Global Affairs Canada sanctions clearance; independent sanctions-verification report; no-match notification from the bank's screening system; legal opinion on beneficial ownership; audited financial statements; and commercial purpose documentation evidencing lawful trade in virgin polyethylene/polypropylene granules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth for the initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital call resolution; certified corporate resolutions; source-of-funds declaration; bank reference letters and six-month bank statements from the parent entity; executed commercial contracts; invoices and bills of lading; tax filings; and notarized statements explaining the commercial rationale for the injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) relationship or reputation-risk flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced KYC questionnaire; declaration of political exposure; independent adverse-media and asset-verification report; legal opinion on PEP status; confirmation of day-to-day treasury management by non-PEP officers; and documentary proof of legitimate merchant/trading counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume USD or FX disbursements to high-risk foreign trade counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file: purchase orders, MT103/LC records, transport documents, insurance certificates, HS classification, import/export licences, certificate of analysis for polymer cargo, counterparty CDD and sanctions-clearance certificates, and written confirmation that no transaction touches a prohibited party or country.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 transferred from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Canadian operational account at a tier-1 Canadian bank, quoting in field 70 the payment purpose 'CAPITAL INJECTION / EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' and referencing the corporate treasury number. CAD settlement occurs through Payments Canada's Lynx system (large-value RTGS) or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS); USD funds clear through the Canadian bank's US correspondent account. FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting applies to outgoing or incoming transfers exceeding CAD 10,000. Statistics Canada international investment reporting applies to equity and direct-investment inflows; no exchange-control permit or prior approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For bulk polymer supplier settlements, use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers or irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 (MT700/MT798) with the commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of analysis, and transport insurance as supporting documents. CAD payments clear via Lynx or ACSS; USD payments clear through correspondent banking rails. Treasury must retain the full trade-documentation bundle in order to satisfy bank document checks and any CRA or CBSA audit trail. No Canadian regulatory approval is needed for outward FX remittances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/JPY
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for funding liabilities
Plain-vanilla FX options (bidirectional calls and puts)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies without local deliverability
Forward-ladder programmes with tenors matched to polymer inventory turnover and receivable cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each fiscal year, regardless of incorporation date; if no fiscal year is established, within 60 days of the anniversary of initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a late-update fee and, after 12 consecutive months of non-filing, the Registrar may strike the enterprise registration and administratively dissolve the corporation; directors and officers remain exposed to liability for actions taken while the corporation is not in good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Conditional - Canada Business Corporations Act Annual Return (if the corporation is incorporated under the CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, not the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporations in default for one year may be dissolved by the Director under section 212 of the CBCA; directors may incur personal liability for continued corporate operations after dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end; e.g. June 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equals 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; prescribed interest accrues on unpaid tax; directors may be liable for unremitted payroll and source deductions under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end; e.g. June 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months for late filing; interest at the Tax Administration Act prescribed rate; possible legal hypothec by Revenu Québec for unpaid amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset or revenue threshold creates a mandatory audit for a private Quebec corporation under the QBCA or the CBCA; an auditor may be waived by an annual unanimous shareholder resolution/consent. An audit becomes mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer, if shareholders holding qualifying minority rights require an auditor, or if a bank LC/covenant agreement imposes an independent audit. The bulk petrochemical distribution business, if operated as a private trading entity, does not itself trigger a statutory audit solely from ISIC/NAICS classification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; a private enterprise may elect the Part II Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial statements submitted with the federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 must be prepared in Canadian dollars under the selected framework and include notes if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, the corporation must maintain a register of ultimate beneficiaries identifying every individual with significant control (voting shares, de facto control, or other prescribed indicators). All changes must be recorded in the register within 15 days of the change or of obtaining knowledge thereof. As part of each annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the director/officer must confirm that the register of individuals with significant control has been reviewed and is complete and accurate as of the confirmation date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - 500 per year for registered office/registered agent service in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 35,000 for a mid-sized wholesale trading entity if audit is required; USD 0 if the unanimous waiver applies and no lender/creditor contractually requires audited financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory corporate income tax rate (federal 15% general rate + Quebec 11.5% general rate); federal basic rate of 38% is reduced by the 10% provincial abatement and the 13% general rate reduction
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available to a pure wholesale distributor of petrochemical polymers. The federal Small Business Deduction (reduced 9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) and the Quebec SME reduced rate (3.2%) are unavailable because a company controlled by non-residents is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation. The Quebec tax holiday for large investment projects (10-year exemption for manufacturing projects exceeding CAD 100 million) does not apply to ISIC 4669 trading operations. The 15% federal general rate and 11.5% Quebec general rate constitute the effective rate absent project-based credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed through CRA e-file using certified tax preparation software or via the CRA's EDI transmission service; the T2 return incorporates Schedule 90 (Form T106) for non-arm's-length international transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end. Instalments are due monthly where federal tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000; the final balance of tax is due 2 months after year-end (3 months for Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the small business deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Line 100 — Sales, commissions and receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue as reported in the financial statements, including all proceeds from the wholesale resale of polyethylene and polypropylene granules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all letter-of-credit proceeds and foreign-currency polymer sales converted at the Bank of Canada annual average rate; segregate Canadian domestic sales from export sales for interprovincial and treaty allocation purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Line 300 / Schedule 1 — Taxable income and federal tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income derived from GAAP net income with reconciling adjustments; Schedule 1 computes federal tax at 15% on general taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned corporations must apply the 15% general rate; the small business deduction must not be claimed where the corporation is neither a CCPC nor carrying on an active business in Canada; deduct only arm's-length intercompany costs supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return of reportable non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory filing when the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions with any non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year; disclose polymer purchase volumes, related-party freight, management fees, loans and adjustments for each related enterprise.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; a repeated-failure surcharge of 10% applies to second consecutive late filings; interest at the CRA prescribed rate accrues daily on all unpaid balances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17.T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through Revenu Quebéc's clic ReQ portal or via approved data-transfer software; the provincial return is integrated with the federal tax data.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17.T2 must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance of Quebec tax is due 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations); instalments are monthly for large corporations and quarterly for smaller entities based on prior-year tax payable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17.T2 Division I — Quebec taxable income (Line 200)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of taxable income earned in Quebec, starting from the federal taxable income and applying provincial additions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholesale trading entity with its sole commercial substance in Quebec, allocate 100% of business income to Quebec; ensure full reconciliation with T2 Line 300; no provincial small business deduction if the corporation is not Canadian-controlled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the Quebec income tax at the 11.5% general rate, reduced by available provincial credits and tax instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the general rate; do not claim Quebec SME or innovation credits absent qualifying activity; disclose any Quebec permanent establishment and payroll headcount in the province to support income allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec: penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month of late filing, subject to maximum of 12 months; an additional 10% penalty for repeated failure; interest at the Revenu Quebéc prescribed rate, compounded daily, on all arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; Quebec imposes an additional 15% tax on dividends paid to non-residents, producing a combined gross statutory burden of 40% before treaty relief. Deemed dividends on corporate wind-up or redemption of shares are subject to the same Part XIII treatment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) for the federal freezing or reduction of withholding and Revenu Quebéc Form VP-311 for the provincial component, delivering the forms to the paying corporation before the dividend is paid. The non-resident must obtain an official certificate of residence (TRC) from the residence-jurisdiction tax authority and present it to CRA or Revenu Quebéc upon demand. Treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses must be satisfied, particularly under the Canada-US Treaty Article XXIX-A. The Canadian payer retains the completed forms and reports the dividend and treaty-reduced rate in its T2 information schedules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% on both interest and royalty payments to non-residents. Under the Canada-US Treaty, arm's-length interest is exempt from Canadian withholding (0%), contingent interest is subject to 15%, and most industrial royalties are limited to 10% (0% for certain cultural copyrights); most other Canadian tax treaties reduce interest and royalties to 10%. Quebec's separate provincial withholding on interest and royalties is relieved through the federal-provincial coordination mechanism and the applicable treaty credit, avoiding duplicate economic taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Form T106 reporting when aggregate reportable non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents equal or exceed CAD 1,000,000 in a taxation year. Mandatory contemporaneous Local File documentation must be prepared when aggregate reportable transactions with a non-resident related party equal or exceed CAD 1,000,000 for non-loan transactions or CAD 5,000,000 for financing transactions; the Master File is required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding CAD 1 billion and the Local File threshold is met. All transfer-pricing documentation must exist by the T2 filing due date to demonstrate reasonable efforts and avoid the 10% penalty under ITA s.247(4).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations statute; substance is instead tested through the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s.245), treaty limitation-on-benefits provisions, the CRA sham doctrine, and the permanent-establishment tests under ITA s.253. A Quebec booking company owning no inventory, employing no staff, maintaining no physical premises, and assuming no price risk on bulk polymer resales is exposed to full reassessment, TP adjustment, GAAR denial of treaty benefits, and gross-negligence penalties even though it is legally incorporated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false T2 or CO-17.T2 returns, underreporting polymer sale proceeds, fabricating purchase invoices from related petrochemical suppliers, destroying books and records before the six-year statutory retention period expires, or issuing false certificates of residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s.239: on summary conviction, a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and up to 2 years' imprisonment; on indictment, a fine of 100% to 200% of the tax evaded and up to 5 years' imprisonment. Quebec Tax Administration Act s.102 imposes an additional fine of 100% to 200% of the evaded provincial tax and a term of imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under ITA s.163(2), doubled in Quebec under TAA s.1049, plus daily compounded interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or participate in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid federal and Quebec income tax and Part XIII liabilities; criminal courts impose travel restrictions and may order passport seizure; Canada-US extradition applies to cross-border tax fraud; directors face personal fines equivalent to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a registered agent address, having no employees in Quebec, executing backdated board minutes, and interposing a Quebec invoice company between foreign polymer producers and Canadian buyers solely to divert margin to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA or Revenu Quebéc recharacterizes the transactions as a sham or abusive avoidance, denies all intercompany deductions under GAAR, levies a 50% gross-negligence penalty, applies a 10% transfer-pricing penalty on net adjustments exceeding the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue, and denies treaty benefits under the applicable LOB article; funds may be frozen as proceeds of unlawful activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil where the corporation is a façade; directors become personally liable for all unremitted payroll source deductions and QST under ITA s.227.1 and Quebec TAA s.31.0.1; Quebec enforcement courts may issue an order prohibiting a director from leaving Quebec pending satisfaction of tax arrears; aggravated cases yield personal bankruptcy orders and director disqualification.
